questions.question: A 60-year-old woman from Jamaica presents with T-cell leukemia. What is the most likely associated infection?

parts.text: A 60-year-old woman from Jamaica presents with T-cell leukemia. What is the most likely associated infection?

parts_raw.text: 60F presents with T-cell leukemia from Jamaica. What is the most likely associated infection?

questions.model_answer: HTLV-1 (human T-cell leukemia virus type 1), the etiologic agent of adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma; the Caribbean, including Jamaica, is a major endemic focus (seropositivity 5%-14%).

questions.question: How is HTLV-1 transmitted?

parts.text: How is this infection transmitted?

parts_raw.text: How is this infection transmitted?

questions.model_answer: Three major routes, all cell-associated: (1) Mother-to-child, predominantly through breastfeeding (infected milk-borne lymphocytes) (2) Sexual transmission (heterosexual and male-to-male) (3) Parenteral: transfusion of cellular blood components and injection drug use. (SOT is also reported.)

cohort_answer.text: Breast feeding, sexually, organ donation, blood transfusion. (3)

questions.question: Name 6 different viruses and an associated malignancy with each one.

parts.text: Name 6 different viruses and an associated malignancy with each one.

parts_raw.text: Name 6 different viruses and an associated malignancy with each one

questions.model_answer: (1) Epstein-Barr virus (HHV-4) - Burkitt lymphoma / nasopharyngeal carcinoma. (2) Human herpesvirus 8 (KSHV) - Kaposi sarcoma / primary effusion lymphoma. (3) Human papillomavirus (high-risk, e.g. 16/18) - cervical and oropharyngeal carcinoma. (4) Hepatitis B virus - hepatocellular carcinoma. (5) Hepatitis C virus - hepatocellular carcinoma. (6) Human T-lymphotropic virus type 1 (HTLV-1) - adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma.
questions.beyond_mandell: Cross-virus oncogenic associations (HPV, HBV, HCV, HTLV-1, HHV-8) are established knowledge/IARC classification; only EBV and HHV-8 are covered in this chapter.

questions.question: A woman from the Caribbean presents with T-cell lymphoma.
questions.question_raw: Q31 (2015). Woman from the Caribbean with T cell lymphoma.

parts.text: Viral association?
Three modes of acquisition/transmission?
Other complications of the virus?

parts_raw.text: A) Viral association?
B) 3 modes of acquisition/transmission?
C) Other complications of the virus?

questions.model_answer: a) HTLV-1. b) (1) Vertical/mother-to-child, primarily breastfeeding (2) Sexual transmission (3) Parenteral (transfusion of cellular blood products / injection drug use). c) Neurologic: HAM/tropical spastic paraparesis, sensory neuropathy, ALS-like syndrome. Dermatologic: infective dermatitis, refractory crusted (Norwegian) scabies. Ocular: uveitis, Sjögren-like keratoconjunctivitis. Rheumatologic: polymyositis, arthropathy. Pulmonary: infiltrative pneumonitis/bronchiectasis. Infectious: Strongyloides stercoralis hyperinfection.

cohort_answer.text: A) HTLV-1. B) Vertical transmission (mother to child, primarily breastmilk); Sexual transmission; Parenteral (IVDU or transfusions). C) Neuro: HTLV-associated myelopathy/tropical spastic paraparesis, ALS, peripheral neuropathy. Skin: infective dermatitis, crusted scabies, eczema, seborrheic dermatitis. Eyes: uveitis, keratoconjunctivitis sicca. Rheum: polymyositis. Cancer: Adult T cell leukemia-lymphoma.

parts_raw.text: Name two non-infectious conditions/diseases associated with HTLV-1
Name two infectious diseases/syndromes associated with HTLV-1
What one thing do you suggest to her to prevent vertical transmission

questions.model_answer: a) (1) Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATL) (2) HTLV-1-associated myelopathy/tropical spastic paraparesis (HAM/TSP). b) (1) Strongyloides stercoralis hyperinfection (2) Infective dermatitis (recurrent Staphylococcus/Streptococcus skin infection); refractory crusted scabies also acceptable. c) Avoid breastfeeding (do not breastfeed the infant), the predominant route of mother-to-child transmission.

cohort_answer.text: Non-infectious: Adult T cell leukemia lymphoma (ATLL); HTLV-I-associated myelopathy (HAM), also known as tropical spastic paraparesis (TSP). Infectious: Strongyloides hyperinfection syndrome; TB; Leprosy; Infective dermatitis; Schistosoma mansoni. Prevention of vertical transmission: Avoid breastfeeding; screening of blood donors; safe sex; avoid sharing needles

questions.question: Name 6 different viruses that cause cancer and the type of cancer each causes.

parts.text: Name 6 different oncogenic viruses and the cancer each causes.

parts_raw.text: Name 6 different viruses that cause cancer and what type of cancer?

questions.model_answer: (1) HPV (high-risk 16/18) - cervical, anogenital and oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma. (2) Hepatitis B virus - hepatocellular carcinoma. (3) Hepatitis C virus - hepatocellular carcinoma. (4) Epstein-Barr virus - Burkitt and nasopharyngeal carcinoma (and Hodgkin/post-transplant lymphoma). (5) HHV-8 (KSHV) - Kaposi sarcoma (and primary effusion lymphoma). (6) HTLV-1 - adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma. (Merkel cell polyomavirus - Merkel cell carcinoma is an acceptable additional answer.)
questions.beyond_mandell: Only HPV is covered in this chapter; the other oncogenic viruses are from established virology (Mandell general/oncovirus chapters).
